coverage_note: Read in full: spec lines 242-348 and 603-1711; code base.py (all 1405 lines), gaussian.py, wiener.py, inverse_gaussian.py, gamma.py, rainflow.py, and config.py _derive, _quad_coefficients, _cap, _check_ranges, _check_models, _check_state, _masks, load_config. Checked row by row: coefficients, big-M constants, days, cells, variable bounds, build conditions, indicator form, tangent and pwl forms (P=1 and P>=2), NonConvex, three objective modes, z rows, loop rows, damage penalty. Numerical checks run outside Gurobi (numpy/scipy only): ig_mean_cap against scipy.stats.invgauss and quad (4 cases, agreement to 1e-13); sharp_cap against a brute-force w(A) on a grid of 200001 values of c (7 cases, w(A_1) <= eps within 1e-9 and w((1+1e-6)A_1) > eps). No wrong_logic, missing_implementation or partial_implementation found: every row of the spec section is built by the code with the stated coefficients, constants and days, and the code builds no row and no variable that the spec does not list. Only undocumented behaviour remains (low severity).

issues.spec_reference: spec.tex lines 259-263: "prepare(ctx, cfg, cells, opts): ... stores the per-cell arrays of the model in ctx, creates the variables of the tracked quantities other than the shared mean mu, and of the anchors and selectors, of these cells only ..."; "The context ctx holds the sizes F, L, M, H_1, H_2, T; the Gurobi model; the shared variables ...; the per-cell arrays (model, tau, epsilon, rho, initial and replacement values, starting anchors); the increment accessor ...; the run options; a dictionary extras." Line 1315 documents ctx.extras["gamma"] only.
issues.location: src/fleet_management/degradation_model/base.py lines 60-105 (FleetModel), 623-646 (build_context), 696-709 (add_pwl_vars); gaussian.py line 41; wiener.py lines 41-44; inverse_gaussian.py lines 94-98; rainflow.py lines 115-116; gamma.py line 169
issues.description: The spec lists what prepare creates as 'tracked quantities, anchors and selectors', but prepare also creates the segment binaries w (base.add_pwl_vars, called by the Gaussian, Wiener and rainflow prepare at the cells with a quadratic row in the pwl form). The spec's list of ctx contents is shorter than the code's: ctx also holds the per-cell selectors repair_of, bound_of, impl_of, encoding_of; tangent_ref; the natural ranges state_range (keys mu, v, R, K, read from cfg.range_mu, range_v, range_R, range_K); pwl_points; allow_replacement; the profiles dictionary behind the increment accessor; and the variable registries state_vars, anchor_vars (q -> {(i,l,k): Var}), nb (selector n) and pwl_w (segment binaries w). ctx.extras has these keys, which the spec does not name: extras['gaussian'] = {v_max_user}; extras['wiener'] = {sigma, v_max_user}; extras['inverse_gaussian'] = {mu_bar per cell, computed once in prepare by ig_mean_cap}; extras['rainflow'] = {rows: constants of the reliability row per cell}; only extras['gamma'] is documented (beta_star and cap). A reader who adds a model, or plans a change, needs these names.
issues.suggested_fix: In spec 259 add 'and the segment binaries w' to the list of variables that prepare creates. In spec 263 add the missing ctx members (the four selector arrays, tangent_ref, the natural ranges, pwl_points, allow_replacement, the registries state_vars, anchor_vars, nb, pwl_w). Add one sentence (or one table row per model) giving the content of ctx.extras for each model: gaussian {v_max_user}, wiener {sigma, v_max_user}, inverse_gaussian {mu_bar}, rainflow {rows}, gamma {beta_star, cap}.

issues.spec_reference: spec.tex lines 257-272: "A builder has the attribute name and three hooks ... add_cell(ctx, i, l): adds the rows of one cell (Section constraints): dynamics in the form of encoding, replacement and anchor rows, repair-cost rows, reliability rows in the form of reliability_impl, loop rows of the full tracked state." and line 272: "A model is added by a module with its builder, its registration, its input checks in config.py and its section in this specification."
issues.location: src/fleet_management/degradation_model/base.py lines 654-950: repair_factor, add_state_vars, add_selector_vars, add_pwl_vars, mission_count, day_increment, add_selector_rows, add_quantity_rows (with repair_keeps_state), add_repair_cost_rows, add_upper_cap_rows, add_quadratic_reliability_rows; comment at lines 715-717 gives the call order
issues.description: Every builder in the code assembles its rows from one set of shared helpers in base.py, in a fixed order (add_selector_rows; add_quantity_rows once per tracked quantity with mu first; the reliability rows; add_repair_cost_rows). The spec does not mention the helpers or the order. Two behaviours live only in the helpers and are visible nowhere else in the spec text: (a) add_quantity_rows builds the loop rows of the quantity and of its anchor (Eq. a_loop) inside the dynamics helper, so a new builder that skips it has no loop row; (b) add_quadratic_reliability_rows builds the side row mu <= mu_side for all three forms and falls back to the single tangent at tau/2 when form = pwl and P = 1 (documented in 919-920, but as a property of the row, not of the helper). The spec says the interface is the three hooks; in fact a new model must also call the helpers to get the rows that Section 'Constraints' requires. The 'loop rows of the full tracked state' in line 260 is the only hint.
issues.suggested_fix: Add to the Cell-Builder Interface (after line 262) a short list of the helper functions of base.py with one line each (what they create, which spec equations), and the order in which add_cell calls them. State that add_quantity_rows also builds the loop rows.

issues.spec_reference: spec.tex lines 1124-1126 (inverse Gaussian) and 1317-1319 (Gamma): "The module imports base under a guard: without gurobipy it loads, base is None and no builder is registered." Nothing equivalent is stated in the Rainflow section (1322-1559).
issues.location: src/fleet_management/degradation_model/rainflow.py lines 21-27 (guarded import), 49-78 (row_constants), 158 (registration only if base is not None)
issues.description: rainflow.py has the same guarded import as inverse_gaussian.py and gamma.py and a public function row_constants(bound, tau, eps, b, s) that returns the constants of the reliability row of every bound (q, c2, c1, mu_side for the quadratic rows; q, cap for Markov and Chernoff: cap = eps*tau and s*tau + ln(eps)). The module loads without gurobipy and registers no builder then. The spec documents the guard and the stand-alone functions for the inverse Gaussian and Gamma modules only, because config.py imports their caps. For rainflow the spec gives the constants only as equations (rf_markov to rf_chernoff and the table at 1544-1548); row_constants and the dispatch table BOUND_QUANTITY (bound -> tracked quantity, increment profile, squared) are not described. The constants agree with the spec (checked: Cantelli c2 = eps/(1-eps); Hoeffding c2 = 2/kappa; Bernstein c2 = 1/(2 kappa), c1 = -b/3, side tau - kappa*b/3; Chernoff cap = s*tau - kappa), so this is only a missing description.
issues.suggested_fix: In the Rainflow section, after the table of tracked quantities (line 1375), add: the module rainflow.py imports base under the same guard; row_constants gives the constants of the reliability row per bound without Gurobi; the table maps each bound to its tracked quantity, its increment profile (support is squared for Hoeffding) and its row.
